articles.title: We check 50,000 paid x402 endpoints every day. Here's what works and what breaks.
articles.excerpt: x402 lets an API ask for payment with an HTTP 402 Payment Required answer, so an AI agent can pay per call in stablecoins without an account or API key. Before an agent pays an endpoint it has never s…
articles.body: x402 lets an API ask for payment with an HTTP 402 Payment Required answer, so an AI agent can pay per call in stablecoins without an account or API key. Before an agent pays an endpoint it has never seen, it wants to know two things: will the payment go through, and will it get what it paid for? x402 Doctor checks that for every paid endpoint we can find, every day. This is what the October data shows (scan of 17 October 2026, live numbers ). In short: 50,373 paid endpoints checked on 17 Oct (x402 and MPP) 93% payable as advertised 41% of all payable endpoints belong to one seller $0.01 median price per call 1. Most endpoints work Of the 50,373 endpoints that answered on 17 October, 46,906 (93.1%) were payable as listed.

articles.title: AgentSCM - Catch agent merge conflicts at edit time, not merge time.
articles.excerpt: Today we're soft-launching the alpha version of AgentSCM for preview and testing. Sub-agents and other team mates contributing to the same source git repo can cause issues not seen until merge or PR t…
articles.body: Today we're soft-launching the alpha version of AgentSCM for preview and testing. Sub-agents and other team mates contributing to the same source git repo can cause issues not seen until merge or PR time. There are still questions on whether the usual git workflow survives automated agentic coding long-term, but in the interim we are building AgentSCM to build a community of builders looking to work together, as native as possible embedded in their daily workspace(s), to catch conflicts between sub-agents and other contributors' agents in real-time. At the edit : before an agent edits a file, its hook asks a local hub who else holds it. The first overlapping edit isn't applied, and the agent is told who holds the file and their task.

articles.title: Magnitude vs Ollama: Hardware-Tuned Kernels Cut Inference Latency in Half
articles.excerpt: The Problem: Ollama's One-Size-Fits-All Kernel Leaves Performance on the Table Running a 70B model on heterogeneous hardware exposes Ollama's core architectural constraint: it ships pre-compiled GGML…
articles.body: The Problem: Ollama's One-Size-Fits-All Kernel Leaves Performance on the Table Running a 70B model on heterogeneous hardware exposes Ollama's core architectural constraint: it ships pre-compiled GGML kernels optimized for generic x86/ARM profiles. Your M2 Max, RTX 4090, or AMD 7950X all run the same matrix multiplication routines, ignoring chip-specific SIMD widths, cache hierarchies, and memory bandwidth characteristics. The symptom: identical models produce wildly different time-to-first-token (TTFT) and tokens-per-second across nominally similar hardware configs. Worse, KV-cache thrashing under long contexts (8K+) can degrade throughput by 40% as the static memory allocator fails to adapt to your actual VRAM/RAM split.

articles.excerpt: By Mansour Jabinpour. Originally published on LumoWP. Republished by LumoWP. WPML TROUBLESHOOTING A French page opens, but the header is still English. A translation says “complete,” yet the language…
articles.body: By Mansour Jabinpour. Originally published on LumoWP . Republished by LumoWP. WPML TROUBLESHOOTING A French page opens, but the header is still English. A translation says “complete,” yet the language switcher refuses to show it. Or the shop works perfectly until a customer changes language at checkout. These are different failures, even when they all look like “WPML is not translating.” The useful question is where the translation stopped: creating the content, publishing it, choosing the correct language, rendering a template, or delivering a cached response. Changing settings at every layer makes that question harder to answer. Start with one affected URL and one language pair.

articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
